cryptic

/KRIP-tik/ — stress on KRIP · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Cryptic describes something whose meaning is mysterious or hard to figure out, as if written in a puzzle on purpose.

Her cryptic reply — 'you'll see on Friday' — only deepened the mystery.

Worked Example

The ancient painting contained cryptic symbols in its corners that scholars debated for decades before anyone proposed a convincing interpretation.

Crypt (hidden) + -ic (having the characteristic of) = having the characteristic of being hidden. The symbols' meaning is deliberately concealed or obscured, embodying that sense of hidden mystery.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

obscure: Obscure means hard to understand or little known - an obscure reference sails past most readers simply because they lack the background. Cryptic implies intent: a cryptic message seems designed to hide its meaning, like a puzzle. Obscure things happen to be unclear; cryptic things are made that way.

enigmatic: Enigmatic means deeply puzzling, like a riddle - an enigmatic smile invites endless guessing and never confirms an answer. Cryptic is more pointed and deliberate: a cryptic remark is compressed and coded on purpose. A person can be enigmatic without trying; a cryptic hint is engineered to conceal.

mysterious: Mysterious means unexplained in a way that stirs wonder - a mysterious light in the sky, a mysterious stranger. Cryptic is narrower: it describes messages and signs whose meaning is hidden as if on purpose. Events and people are mysterious; a deliberately vague clue is cryptic.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

explicit: stated fully and clearly, nothing left hidden

straightforward: direct and easy to understand

Where it sits · how deliberately the meaning is hidden — unclear → confusing → puzzling → cryptic

unclear vs. cryptic: Unclear directions leave out a detail or two, but a cryptic note seems designed to hide its meaning entirely.

confusing vs. cryptic: A confusing map can be figured out with patience, while a cryptic riddle guards its meaning like a secret.

puzzling vs. cryptic: Her puzzling reply made me think for a moment, but his cryptic one-word answer left the whole room in the dark.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — crypt

Root — crypt: hidden — from Greek kryptos; the same crypt as the hidden underground burial chamber beneath a church (Greek)

Suffix — -ic

Suffix — -ic: characteristic of; having the nature of (Greek (via Latin -icus))

Put it together

Put it together: crypt- (hidden) + -ic (characteristic of) = having the nature of something hidden. A cryptic message keeps its meaning buried out of sight — just like a crypt hides a chamber beneath a church.

Use the root in a new word: encrypt

Use the root in a new word: encrypt: Banks encrypt your account information so that thieves who intercept it see only scrambled nonsense.

Word Choice

neutral

Use cryptic when something is deliberately hard to understand—like a coded message, a mysterious hint, or a puzzle designed to confuse. Reserve it for contexts where the mystery or hiddenness is intentional or structural, not accidental confusion.
